skills.name: Responses to German rule: resistance and protest

note.text: Resistance to German expansion included armed defence, petitions and refusal of imposed demands. Bakweri, Bangwa, Mamfe/Cross River and Nso campaigns had distinct causes and sequences. Early coastal conflict must also be separated from the later Duala land protest associated with Rudolf Duala Manga Bell. Compare demand, response and consequence, keeping African decisions visible. An official label such as rebellion does not prove that a community had freely accepted colonial authority. A military defeat did not erase continuing opposition or the costs of colonial rule.

sections.heading: Coastal and Bakweri responses
sections.text: Lock Priso’s opposition in {1884} differed from later Duala land petitions. Rudolf Duala Manga Bell challenged expropriation and was executed in {1914}. Around Buea, Kuva Likenye defended Bakweri authority and land against intrusion. His forces repelled the German attack in {1891}; a better-armed attack in {1894} defeated them. An early victory did not ensure permanent independence.

sections.heading: Bangwa: recruitment and changing relations
sections.text: Asunganyi initially received Gustav Conrau, who recruited workers for coastal plantations in {1898}. When Conrau sought more workers without the earlier recruits returning, relations deteriorated. Conrau was detained and died after attempting escape; accounts differ about the precise circumstances. Bangwa resistance met repeated German raids, destruction and seizures. Asunganyi continued opposition before his capture and exile in {1911}. Initial cooperation did not mean unconditional consent.

sections.heading: Mamfe and the Upper Cross River
sections.text: Colonial intrusion, coercion and commercial demands provoked opposition among communities around the Cross River. In {1904}, Pückler-Limpurg’s expedition met armed resistance; he died during the fighting. Attacks also targeted trading posts. German forces retaliated through destructive campaigns, including burning settlements and crops and executing opponents. Colonial control followed severe repression. Mamfe is a regional label here, not proof that every community had one ruler or identical aims.

sections.heading: Nso: distinguish the encounters
sections.text: Nso defended its authority amid unequal colonial demands. Pavel’s armed presence must be distinguished from Houben’s attack in {1902} and the further campaign in {1906}, after which German control and tribute demands were imposed. The palace suffered burning and looting during military violence. Ngonnso’s removal has a contested acquisition history: do not assign it to a particular battle without evidence. Compare local memory and colonial records, then explain each campaign’s causes, methods and consequences.
